clue.text: Miserable thing — article has nothing going for it

indicators.note: one letter going for another stands in its place, so the article takes over from the nothing

parts.note: an object is a thing
nothing is zero, the letter O
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A wretched item, with a grammatical article that has nothing in its favour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going for' means replacing: the A (article) replaces the O (nothing) in OBJECT. 'has nothing going for it' reads like a phrase about having no merits.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe a wretched, hopeless state, as in abject poverty: a synonym.

clue.text: Hold rude cartoons found in B&B

indicators.note: the scrambled letters are found in, so placed inside, the two Bs

parts.note: B&B, bed and breakfast, supplies the two letters B and B

indicators.note: rude here means crude or rough, so the letters of the word cartoons are roughly rearranged

explanation.surface: Smutty comic strips discovered at a bed-and-breakfast guesthouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rude' signals the anagram and 'found in' the insertion; 'Hold' looks like a verb but is a wrestling grip.
explanation.definitionFit: A Boston crab is a wrestling hold in which the opponent's legs are bent back over their body.

clue.text: Additional matter written about lake

indicators.note: something written about another wraps round it, so the matter surrounds the lake

parts.note: pus is matter discharged from a wound
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: Extra material has been composed concerning a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'matter' looks like subject matter, but it is pus; 'written about' puts PUS round L.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means extra or additional, as in a plus point: a synonym.

clue.text: A Republican state, one of the old Confederate ones

definitions.text: one of the old Confederate ones

parts.note: Kansas is a US state

explanation.surface: A Republican-leaning state that was among those which seceded in the American Civil War.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' is both the wordplay's KANSAS and the theme of the definition, which points to the eleven states of the Civil War Confederacy.
explanation.definitionFit: This southern state seceded in 1861 and joined the Confederacy: an example of the group.

clue.text: Drink a party knocked over onto suit

indicators.note: the overturned piece is placed onto, so after, the suit

parts.note: clubs is one of the four suits in a pack of cards

indicators.note: something knocked over is turned upside down, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: At a party, someone's drink has been knocked over and spilt onto their suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' signals reversal and 'onto' puts that piece after the card suit; 'suit' is not clothing here.
explanation.definitionFit: It is carbonated water used as a mixer, a kind of beverage.

clue.text: Sucker, having tablet during game, flipped

indicators.note: flipped means turned over, so the assembled letters are read in reverse
the tablet is taken during the game, so it goes inside it

parts.note: pool is a cue game
a pill is a tablet

explanation.surface: A dupe who took a pill mid-game and then lost it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' signals insertion and 'flipped' reverses the whole result; 'Sucker' looks like a dupe but is a sweet on a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet on a stick is sucked, so a sucker is a playful name for it.

clue.text: Frazzled, make amends before cards put in post

indicators.note: the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: to atone is to make amends

indicators.note: the cards are put in the post, so they go inside it

parts.note: to post a letter is to send it
cards are comical people, wits

explanation.surface: Someone harassed apologises and then mails some greeting cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cards' means witty characters, not playing or greeting cards; 'put in' signals insertion and 'before' the order.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at the end of one's resources of patience is an idiom for being exasperated and worn out.

clue.text: Nervously trail a rope

indicators.note: acting nervously means moving jumpily, so the letters of these words are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Anxiously drag a rope behind you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nervously' rearranges TRAILA.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso used by cowboys for catching cattle is a kind of rope.

clue.text: Partner's second to leave girl

indicators.note: the letter is made to leave the name, so it is taken out

parts.note: Sally is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A boyfriend's second date is about to walk out on a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' looks like an ordinal, but it is S, the time unit's abbreviation; removing it from SALLY leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A partner in a joint enterprise or alliance is a confederate: a synonym.

clue.text: Customer's legal right in court

indicators.note: the legal right goes in the court, inside its letters

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to keep property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A buyer's legal entitlement being argued before a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals insertion; the possessive 's on 'Customer' is just a link meaning has.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who buys services from a professional or business is their customer: a synonym.

clue.text: Old British ruined castle, something standing in the way of progress

definitions.text: something standing in the way of progress

indicators.note: a ruined building has fallen apart, so the letters of the word castle tumble into a new order

explanation.surface: An old ruined British castle blocks the route of a new development.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' signals the anagram, which reads naturally as describing the castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A hindrance or barrier that blocks advancement fits a thing that stands in the way.

clue.text: Old poet's taken round important north-eastern town

indicators.note: the poet's name is taken round the other pieces, so they sit inside it

parts.note: John Milton was a 17th-century English poet; with the possessive S
key means important, as in a key figure

explanation.surface: A historic poet is given a tour of a significant town in the north-east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken round' signals insertion. The town is in Buckinghamshire, England, not in the north-east at all.
explanation.definitionFit: This large planned settlement in Buckinghamshire, England, is an example of a town.

clue.text: Good entering with nothing on — twice a sexual innuendo implied?

indicators.note: the whole assembled piece is written twice in a row
the letter for good enters, so it goes inside, the word for naked

parts.note: with nothing on means naked, nude

explanation.surface: Something decent getting into a naked body, a suggestive remark twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' puts G inside NUDE, and 'twice' doubles it. The phrase is a catchphrase from Monty Python, a British comedy series.
explanation.definitionFit: The doubled phrase is said with a wink to hint at something sexual, an idiom for innuendo.

clue.text: Pay for extra work during an unspecified period

definitions.meaning: wages paid for hours worked beyond the normal ones
split into two words, the phrase means gradually, across some length of time

explanation.surface: Wages for additional hours, earned over an unstated stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as one word it is extra pay; read as two it means across a span of time.

clue.text: The two in Cabot House

indicators.note: the answer sits in these words, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: The pair living in a building called Cabot House.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points inside CABOT HOUSE, where the letters run across the word break.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means the one and the other together, a pair taken as a unit: a synonym.

clue.text: Intellectual argument in support of very important bishop

indicators.note: in a down clue the support goes beneath, so this piece comes after the others

parts.note: high means very important, as in high priority
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a row is an argument

explanation.surface: A clever debate that backs a senior churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in support of' puts ROW under HIGH + B in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with refined cultural or scholarly tastes is described with this word, a synonym.

clue.text: Took part in boat race, perhaps, and argued

definitions.text: Took part in boat race, perhaps
definitions.meaning: pulled oars in a race on water, the past tense of to row a boat
quarrelled, the past tense of the other sense of row, rhyming with cow

explanation.surface: Someone competed in a rowing contest and also got into a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: The same spelling covers pulled oars and had a quarrel, two words with different sounds.

clue.text: Store for later use in bar

definitions.meaning: to keep something back, to put aside
except, as in all bar one

explanation.surface: Keep supplies in a pub for a later time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub but is the preposition meaning except.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to keep aside and also except, as in all but one.

clue.text: Obey top management, or be overlooked

definitions.meaning: read literally, to follow the rules set by the company's board of directors
the idiom for being neglected or abandoned

explanation.surface: Either follow what the directors say or find yourself passed over.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase means following the directors; as an idiom it means being discarded or ignored.

clue.text: Bird in consequence rising over quarry

indicators.note: in a down clue over puts the first piece above the second
in a down clue rising means read upwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: so means therefore, in consequence
prey is a hunted animal, quarry

explanation.surface: A bird ascends above its prey as a result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' signals reversal in a down entry, and 'over' places that piece above the next.
explanation.definitionFit: The fish-eating hawk is an example of a bird of prey.

clue.text: Mostly happy to host a social event

indicators.note: the host holds a guest inside, so the shortened word surrounds the letter A
most of the word is used, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: glad means happy

explanation.surface: Largely pleased to throw a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' trims GLAD to GLA, and 'to host' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A festive celebration or special occasion, such as a gala dinner, is an example of a social event.

clue.text: Crowd carried east for rally

parts.note: to jam is to crowd or cram together
bore is the past tense of bear, to carry

explanation.surface: A throng carried eastward towards a demonstration.
explanation.definitionFit: A large gathering, especially of Scouts, is a kind of rally or get-together.

clue.text: Rotten trick deleting page

indicators.note: deleting means the letter for page is taken out of the trick

parts.note: a prank is a trick

explanation.surface: A nasty practical joke that involves removing a page.
explanation.definitionFit: Something foul-smelling or utterly bad, putrid, is described as rotten.

clue.text: Outstanding, a Parisian apartment I secured

parts.note: un is French for a, as a Parisian would say it

indicators.note: the apartment holds the letter secure inside it

parts.note: a pad is slang for a flat or apartment

explanation.surface: An excellent Paris flat that I managed to obtain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' means still owed, not excellent; 'secured' puts I inside PAD.
explanation.definitionFit: An outstanding bill is one still owed, not yet settled: a synonym.

clue.text: Primate beginning to bestow a blessing

indicators.note: the beginning of the word bestow is its first letter

parts.note: a boon is a blessing or benefit

explanation.surface: A senior bishop starts to give a benediction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' suggests an archbishop, which fits the blessing, but here it is an ape or monkey.
explanation.definitionFit: This large African monkey is an example of a primate.

clue.text: Bank associated with the Spanish nonsense

parts.note: Dogger Bank is a large sandbank in the North Sea
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A financial institution linked with Spain talks rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' is not a lender but Dogger Bank, a North Sea sandbank familiar from the BBC's shipping forecast.
explanation.definitionFit: Clumsy, badly written verse is meant here, loosely called rubbish.
